title: Detecting Silent Faults at the Environment-Trainer Boundary in Reinforcement Learning
why: B-type evaluation methodology for embodied RL harness integrity: shows learning-curve outcome checks miss silent wire-protocol faults at the environment–trainer boundary, while dual-side step ledgers catch and locate them (incl. 7-joint arm Pusher).
mechanism: Treat env–trainer boundary as an explicit wire protocol; inject silent faults into crossed values / trainer logs; compare outcome-based detectors (learning-curve thresholds, multi-seed comparisons, final-policy eval) vs run-integrity checks (bilateral step ledger, episode record).
evaluation_signal: Author-reported (abstract): unless every value wrong, curve threshold ≤1/10 runs and 10-seed compare ≤21%; of 728 boundary-fault runs both curve checks passed, 723 scored ≤3σ below fault-free seeds; bilateral step ledger caught/located every crossed fault (Pendulum/Hopper/Pusher; Pendulum cross-machine) with ~3% median training-time overhead on Pendulum.
